## Functions

<table><thead><tr><th>

Function


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

[analyzeGraph(graph, options)](./core.analyzegraph.md)


</td><td>

Analyze a migration graph for connectivity, field profiles, and potential issues.

This performs a comprehensive analysis of the entire migration graph, checking for: - Version connectivity (can all versions reach each other?) - Field preservation patterns (which fields are preserved and how often?) - Potential issues (disconnected components, multi-value fields, etc.)


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[analyzeIncremental(graph, \_previousResult, \_changedFiles)](./core.analyzeincremental.md)


</td><td>

Perform incremental analysis by re-analyzing only affected portions of the graph.

This is intended to be more efficient than full analysis when only a small portion of the graph has changed. Currently, this is a stub that delegates to full analysis - true incremental analysis is planned for future implementation.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[createMigrationContext(totalSteps, initialStash)](./core.createmigrationcontext.md)


</td><td>

Create a new migration context for executing a migration path.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[createMigrationGraph(options)](./core.createmigrationgraph.md)


</td><td>

Create a new migration graph.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[findLossyPaths(graph)](./core.findlossypaths.md)


</td><td>

Find all lossy migration paths in the graph.

A lossy path is one where data may be lost during migration, either because: - The migration is explicitly marked as one-way (lossy trait) - Fields are dropped during transformation - Data cannot be perfectly reconstructed when migrating backward

This function analyzes every possible path between version pairs to identify where data loss occurs, which steps are lossy, and why.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[getDeprecatedVersions(graph)](./core.getdeprecatedversions.md)


</td><td>

Get information about deprecated versions and where they're used in migration paths.

This function identifies all versions marked as deprecated in the graph and tracks which migration paths include them. This is useful for: - Planning deprecation timelines - Identifying affected users - Creating migration guides


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[suggestMigrations(graph)](./core.suggestmigrations.md)


</td><td>

Suggest new migrations that would improve graph quality.

This function analyzes the graph to identify opportunities for new migrations that would: - Bridge disconnected version components - Eliminate lossy paths by providing direct, lossless alternatives - Shorten long migration paths with more direct routes

The suggestions are prioritized by impact, with bridging disconnected components being the most critical.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

[calverStrategy](./core.calverstrategy.md)


</td><td>

Calendar versioning strategy. Supports YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY.MM.DD, and YYYYMMDD formats.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[integerStrategy](./core.integerstrategy.md)


</td><td>

Simple integer versioning strategy. Versions are non-negative integers (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3, ...). Leading zeros are not allowed for multi-digit numbers.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[semverStrategy](./core.semverstrategy.md)


</td><td>

Semantic versioning strategy (semver 2.0.0). Supports MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional prerelease and build metadata.


</td></tr>

Profile describing how a field behaves across migration paths.
